title: Rabies Exposure: Risk Assessment and Post-Exposure Prophylaxis
specialty: Infectious Diseases / Emergency Medicine / Public Health

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults and children with a possible rabies exposure from an animal bite, scratch or lick, presenting to the emergency department (ED) or primary care: exposure category, wound washing, rabies vaccine schedules, rabies immunoglobulin (RIG) for category III, previously vaccinated and immunocompromised people. Uses the World Health Organization (WHO) 2017 position summary, the Verorab vaccine product information and the HyperRAB immunoglobulin label. Animal observation, tetanus and antibiotic decisions follow local protocols.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-22.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: No Saudi MOH rabies post-exposure guideline could be opened; national supply of vaccine and immunoglobulin products must be checked locally.
WHO recommends the 1-week 2-site intradermal regimen but the summary opened gives no intradermal volume, so only intramuscular schedules are listed.
WHO lists a 4-dose intramuscular schedule; the Verorab label lists a 5-dose Essen schedule; both are shown.
Observation of the biting dog or cat, tetanus prophylaxis and antibiotics were not covered in the opened sources.
Equine RIG (maximum 40 IU/kg) is mentioned by WHO but no product label was opened.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.

pathophysiology.summary: Rabies is always fatal once symptoms appear, so there is no contraindication to post-exposure prophylaxis (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.3). Risk depends on contact type: licks on intact skin carry no risk; nibbles and minor scratches without bleeding are category II; transdermal bites or scratches are category III (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories). Immunoglobulin gives immediate local antibody at the wound while vaccine antibody develops; it can blunt the vaccine response, so the two are given at different sites (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.5; HyperRAB label, Section Dosage). Vaccine response may be weaker in immunosuppressed people (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.5).

symptoms: History of a bite, scratch or lick from a possibly rabid animal (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories).
Anxiety about exposure; the decision is based on contact type, not symptoms, because rabies is fatal once symptomatic (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.3).
physicalSigns: Transdermal bite or scratch with bleeding: category III (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories).
Minor scratch or abrasion without bleeding: category II (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories).
Intact skin after licking: category I (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories).
redFlags: Category III exposure: start vaccine without delay and give RIG (WHO rabies position 2018, Section RIG).
Immunodeficiency: full course with RIG regardless of category II or III, and antibody check (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Vaccine regimens; Verorab SmPC, Section 4.4).
RIG not given by day 7 after the first vaccine dose: do not give it later (WHO rabies position 2018, Section RIG; HyperRAB label, Section Dosage).
precipitants: Bites or scratches from dogs, cats or wild animals (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories).
Bites on uncovered skin (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories).

clinicalManagement.title: Wash the wound
actions: Wash and flush the wound for about 15 minutes with soap or detergent and plenty of water; apply iodine or another virucidal agent if available (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Wound washing).

clinicalManagement.title: Assign the exposure category
actions: Classify as category I, II or III and check previous vaccination and immune status (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories and Section Vaccine regimens).

clinicalManagement.title: Start the vaccine
actions: Category II and III: start vaccine without delay (see Medicines) (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories).
Resume, do not restart, if a dose is delayed (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Vaccine regimens).

clinicalManagement.title: Give RIG for category III
clinicalManagement.timeframe: With the first vaccine dose, no later than day 7
actions: Infiltrate as much RIG as possible into and around the wound; give any remainder intramuscularly away from the vaccine site (WHO rabies position 2018, Section RIG; HyperRAB label, Section Dosage).
Do not give RIG to previously vaccinated people (WHO rabies position 2018, Section RIG).

clinicalManagement.title: Complete the course
actions: Book every remaining vaccine dose before the patient leaves.
Immunosuppressed: antibody test 2 to 4 weeks after the course (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.4).

regimens.dose: 0.5 mL on days 0, 3, 7 and one dose between days 14 and 28 (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Vaccine regimens); label Essen schedule days 0, 3, 7, 14 and 28 (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.2).
regimens.route: Intramuscular: deltoid in older children and adults, anterolateral thigh in infants and young children; never the buttock
adjustments: PAEDIATRIC: same dose as adults (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.2).

Immunosuppressed, including long-term corticosteroids: full course plus immunoglobulin for category II or III, and check antibodies 2 to 4 weeks after (Verorab SmPC, Sections 4.4 and 4.5; WHO rabies position 2018, Section Vaccine regimens).
If a dose is late, resume the schedule; do not restart (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Vaccine regimens).
No renal or hepatic adjustment stated.
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Anaphylaxis treatment available; fainting after injection (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.4).
Record product name and batch (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.4).
contraindications: No contraindication to post-exposure vaccination because rabies is fatal (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.3).
Caution: allergy to polymyxin B, streptomycin or neomycin; thrombocytopenia or bleeding disorder; phenylketonuria (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.4).
Never in the same syringe or site as immunoglobulin (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.5).

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Touching or feeding animals, licks on intact skin: no prophylaxis (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories).
Nibbling of uncovered skin, minor scratches or abrasions without bleeding: wound washing and vaccine without delay (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories).
Single or multiple transdermal bites or scratches: wound washing, vaccine and RIG (WHO rabies position 2018, Section Exposure categories and Section RIG).
At least two doses of cell-culture vaccine before: two vaccine doses on days 0 and 3, no RIG (Verorab SmPC, Section 4.2; WHO rabies position 2018, Section RIG).

Uses the World Health Organization (WHO) 2017 position summary, the Verorab vaccine product information and the HyperRAB immunoglobulin label. Animal observation, tetanus and antibiotic decisions follow local protocols.
learningObjectives: Give vaccine for category II and III, and RIG for category III.
Adjust for previous vaccination and immunosuppression.
pitfalls: Giving RIG and vaccine at the same site.
Restarting a delayed course instead of resuming.
keyPoints: Rabies is fatal once symptomatic, so never delay prophylaxis.
RIG goes into the wound, not the vaccine site.
No RIG after day 7 or in previously vaccinated people.

patientEducation: Rabies is preventable if treatment starts quickly; keep every vaccine appointment.
Avoid stray or wild animals; seek care after any bite or scratch.
lifestyleAndDiet: Keep pets vaccinated and avoid contact with stray animals.
mdtReferrals: Emergency or primary care physician; infectious diseases; public health for animal follow-up and reporting; pharmacy for vaccine and immunoglobulin supply.
dischargeCriteria: Wound washed and assessed, first vaccine given, RIG given if category III, remaining dose dates booked, return advice given.
